title: Angels send catcher Logan O’Hoppe, reliever Chase Silseth to Rangers ahead of deadline
content:
ANAHEIM, Calif. — Amid a wide-open race in the American League West, the Texas Rangers moved Wednesday to fortify their bullpen and their depth behind the plate, acquiring reliever Chase Silseth and catcher Logan O’Hoppe from the Los Angeles Angels in exchange for infield prospect Angel Arredondo.

The Angels announced the trade, which came days ahead of Monday’s MLB trade deadline.

O’Hoppe was once viewed as a potential franchise cornerstone for the Angels, but the 26-year-old has struggled this season. In 75 games, O’Hoppe has hit .209 with four home runs and a .565 OPS. The Rangers optioned him to Triple-A Round Rock on Wednesday night. The Angels, meanwhile, activated catcher Travis d’Arnaud, who was on the 60-day injured list with right foot plantar fasciitis.

“I thought the best thing for him was going to be a change of scenery,” John Mozeliak, the Angels’ interim GM, said of O’Hoppe. “When you think about catchers, you think about two things: the ability to catch and throw and call a game. The opposite side of that would be the offensive skill set. And he was really struggling, putting a lot of pressure on both sides of the ball. I think that’s really tough to balance. In the end, trying to get him playing time for us was difficult.”

Silseth, 26, had emerged as one of the last-place Angels’ better relievers this season after an uneven start to his career. The right-hander, who averages 96 mph with his fastball and also throws a splitter and sweeper, has a 2.72 ERA, 48 strikeouts and 22 walks in 39 2/3 innings. Silseth, an 11th-round pick in 2021, became the first player from his draft class to reach the majors in 2022. Overall, the former starter has recorded a 4.12 ERA in his big-league career, striking out 153 batters and issuing 70 walks across 139 2/3 innings.

Texas sent 19-year-old infielder Angel Arredondo to the Angels in the deal. The Mexico native has spent the year in Low A, batting .243 with eight home runs and a .763 OPS in 85 games. Arredondo, who was signed for $300,000 by the Rangers in 2024, has mostly played third base and filled in at shortstop.

“As we enter this trading period, one of the things we are focused on is understanding change,” Mozeliak said. “Clearly, where the Angels are at right now, we need to do some things differently. And we are trying to balance having the focus on the future, short term and long term.”
